title: A Semester for the Homecoming
premise: Odile Almeida has one semester left at St. Verity Academy, counting days until they can escape the town, the family bakery, and everyone's assumptions about who they are. Then a group chat called 'The Forecast' begins posting predictions that come true with eerie precision — and Odile realizes the messages are coming from someone who knows them intimately. As the predictions turn from harmless to dangerous and the school fractures around who's behind it, Odile discovers the chat was built on their late grandmother's unfinished experiment in 'emotional forecasting,' an inheritance that chose them without asking. In the end, Odile must decide whether to let the Forecast run out its final prediction — which names them as its author — or destroy the inheritance and claim a future no algorithm wrote for them.
about_author: Ansel Crane is the pen name of a former boarding-school teacher who spent years watching teenagers rehearse versions of themselves for an audience. They write about small towns, big feelings, and the machinery of expectation.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Senior year at St. Verity: Odile bakes lavender bread for a crush they won't name and endures classmates' easy labels — baker's kid, scholarship kid, 'they/them mystery.' The chapter establishes the bakery, the dead grandmother Odile barely remembers, and the suffocating countdown to graduation. Emotional beat: restless longing disguised as indifference.

chapters.title: The First Forecast
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. An unknown number adds Odile to a group chat with five classmates; the first message predicts the gym flood that happens by third period. Panic, thrill, denial. Odile tells no one but starts screenshotting everything. Emotional beat: vertigo — the future suddenly feels like something done to you rather than made by you.

chapters.title: Six Strangers, One Thread
chapters.summary: Rotating POV across the six chat members: jock Theo, overachiever Priya, ghost-quiet Marcus, influencer Wren, burnout Dez, and Odile. Each is hiding something the predictions seem to know. They form a wary alliance to trace the number. Emotional beat: reluctant intimacy — being seen accurately is terrifying and addictive.

chapters.title: What the Bread Knows
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A prediction saves Priya from a car accident, and the school turns worshipful and paranoid at once. Odile notices the forecasts echo phrases from grandmother Rosa Almeida's old recipe journals — marginalia about 'reading what people need before they ask.' Emotional beat: grief resurfacing as curiosity; inheritance as haunting.

chapters.title: Labels
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren leaks screenshots for clout, and the chat goes viral within the school. Everyone gets rebranded by rumor: prophet, fraud, suspect. Odile is publicly outed as connected to the chat and to Rosa's research. Emotional beat: the violence of other people's definitions; power corrupting Wren mid-chapter.

chapters.title: Rosa's Room
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In the bakery basement, Odile finds Rosa's hidden study: decades of forecasting experiments, including a prototype app that ingests personal data to predict behavior — and a final entry addressed to 'whoever inherits this.' The predictions aren't magic; they're surveillance wearing prophecy's clothes. Emotional beat: awe curdling into violation.

chapters.title: The Author Question
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The group turns on each other hunting the sender; Theo, desperate to control his own predicted downfall, secretly feeds the chat more data to steer outcomes. A forecast names Odile as the author. Even allies waver. Emotional beat: betrayal as mirror — everyone wants the power, no one wants the blame.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The final forecast appears: it predicts the bakery burning down during graduation week, with Odile inside. Odile races to find the sender — Marcus, Rosa's other grandchild, raised apart, who inherited half the archive and believes finishing the Forecast honors her. Emotional beat: confrontation between two readings of the same inheritance.

chapters.title: The Last Proof
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Odile and Marcus. Graduation eve: Marcus triggers the final sequence to force the prophecy true; Odile chooses to break the loop instead, publicly dismantling the Forecast and exposing how it manipulated all of them. The fire is prevented, but the truth costs Odile the clean exit they wanted. Emotional beat: climax — agency exercised at maximum price.

chapters.title: Day One
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Aftermath: friendships bruised but real, Wren facing consequences, Marcus beginning repair work, the archive sealed or shared on Odile's terms. At graduation, Odile bakes bread with no message in it at all — just good bread — and walks offstage into an unwritten summer. Emotional beat: quiet triumph; identity claimed, not assigned.
